Paired variables and stationary parameters

A real stationary point can move smoothly with a parameter. A particularly useful phase pairs two sets of variables: Its critical point in is always explicit, even when itself has degenerate critical points. The mixed derivative expansion of this integral has a different ordering from an expansion in integer inverse powers. Counting both orders gives a precise remainder with a fixed number of amplitude derivatives.

We use , the Fourier kernel , and positive frequencies . Here , with ; the parameter ranges over a fixed compact subset of . The case simply omits parameters. Write Every amplitude has support in a fixed compact set. Constants may depend on that set and finitely many phase derivatives, but not on the amplitude or frequency.

Earlier proofs used here

  • Finite stationary jets and quadratic exchange, Theorems 1 and 3, proves the exact complex quadratic estimate and the finite stationary expansion, including its coefficient formula, derivative counts, determinant branch and uniform constants.
  • The complete smooth inverse and implicit maps, §§16.4–16.5, IV1–IV10, supplies the real critical branch. These are earlier AN-03 programme proofs.
  • When a kernel is smooth proves integral Taylor remainders. The scalar foundation, §§12–13, supplies compactness, cutoffs, finite derivative rules and integration by parts. The integration foundation, §§15.0–15.1, supplies Fubini and dominated convergence.
  • Point sources and complex Gaussian kernels, Section 2, proves real symmetric diagonalization. The finite algebra foundation, §10, supplies the determinant, matrix and dimension arguments.
